codeReview.summary: The fix directly addresses the original blocking defect: formatDate no longer uses UTC parsing for date-only strings and now constructs a local date from parsed components, preventing day-shift rendering in non-UTC timezones. The update is scoped, and regression tests were added for date formatting behavior.

issues.description: The regression test validates expected outputs but does not force a negative-offset timezone (where the prior bug manifests), so it may not fail against the old implementation on UTC/positive-offset environments. The code fix is correct, but the test is not timezone-deterministic across all runner environments.

sharedStateObservations.observation: frontend-worker procedure appears stricter than actual practice/enforcement for small frontend fixes: it mandates agent-browser manual verification and shared-state updates, but both the original and fix worker transcripts completed successfully without agent-browser invocation and without updating shared library docs.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/skills/frontend-worker/SKILL.md:43-51 requires manual verification with agent-browser and updating .factory/library/architecture.md; transcript skeletons for worker sessions 5afea2bb-0e18-4111-8d7e-7d2f73911df1 and d48cf499-eba4-4ab7-88dd-e2aeea41bb0d contain no `"skill": "agent-browser"` tool call and handoffs still mark followedProcedure=true.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The shared architecture library still lacks an explicit frontend guideline for timezone-safe formatting of backend LocalDate strings, despite this bug and fix.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Fix commit 4e91106 changes frontend/src/utils/formatters.ts and adds frontend/src/__tests__/formatters.test.ts, but .factory/library/architecture.md contains no corresponding LocalDate/date-formatting convention.

summary: Re-run review passed: the timezone date-formatting fix resolves the original blocking issue from transactions-frontend-ui, and the implementation is correctly scoped with added utility regression coverage.
